context.clinical_context_summary: 80-year-old male with a past medical history of CAD s/p CABG, angina, aortic stenosis (rheumatic/nonrheumatic), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, prior NSTEMI, acute diastolic heart failure, prior sepsis with acute kidney injury, OSA, and multiple orthopedic pain/limited mobility issues; on aspirin 81 mg and supplements. Presents with fever. Risks: high risk for sepsis/clinical deterioration due to age and prior sepsis/AKI; limited cardiovascular reserve (CAD/CABG, aortic stenosis, HFpEF) with potential for demand ischemia/arrhythmia; baseline low blood pressures suggest possible chronic hypotension or frailty—avoid aggressive BP lowering; OSA may predispose to hypoxemia. Current vitals show tachycardia and fever with relatively low SBP/DBP—monitor for shock and end-organ hypoperfusion.
context.rationale: Thresholds are tightened/adjusted to this patient’s observed baseline: SBP averages ~87 with lows to 72, so normal SBP is set lower than standard while keeping conservative warning/critical cutoffs for shock. Cardiovascular comorbidities (CAD/CABG, aortic stenosis, HFpEF) make tachycardia and hypotension more concerning; thus HR normal capped at 100 and warning at 110. SpO2 baseline mean 95 with nadir 92, so normal set ≥94 and warning at 92 to flag decompensation while allowing up to 100 as normal. Temperature distribution (mean 38.1, max 39.1) suggests true fever measurements (not systematically low axillary), so fever warning begins at 38.5 with normal up to 38.0 given chief complaint.
